steps.domain_action: raw food product occupies the void state before any microwave energy enters the chamber.
oven cavity wall closes and contains the radiation field and product volume.
microwave radiation propagates forward from the source into the extended three-dimensional food volume.
penetration couples to absorption which couples to conversion in a sequential chain through the material.
the food product retains its material identity while internal states change.
incident energy opens into two arms, dielectric heating of water and dipolar heating of fats.
water arm affirms constructive heating and moisture migration.
water arm fails where cold spots block energy deposition.
fat arm affirms lipid heating and localized temperature rise.
fat arm fails where insufficient coupling leaves regions unprocessed.
overcooked edge and undercooked center coexist as a live contradiction without resolution.
the two arms rejoin into a composite thermal and chemical state distribution across the product.
heated molecules relax backward toward ambient equilibrium after the source withdraws.
protein denaturation and bond-level alteration are fixed as permanent append-only records.
bridge composition links transformation steps across the Gaussian moat resolution.
bridge existence confirms a path through the moat for energy transfer.
moat versus bridge type mismatch blocks transfer in isolated regions.
successful bridge composition and blocked moat transfer hold both at once.
conflicting bridge and moat observations rejoin to a single system state.
the sealed cavity reasserts the terminal boundary after processing completes.
system-wide heating chains local absorption events into a whole-product pattern.
interaction with any susceptible molecule affirms broad chemical accessibility.
deterministic geometry-enforcing transfer fails where absorption is probabilistic.
achiral mirror-image accessibility and directed source-to-food polarity hold both at once.
the measurement record of temperature and chemical change is append-only and cannot be undone.
